summary.headline: The Board of Health approved a Title 5 variance for 250 Turnpike Road and reviewed FY28 budget scenarios.
summary.summary: The Board of Health heard a presentation on new Massachusetts regulations banning kratom sales and received an update on town compliance. The board voted to approve its $450 elected member budget for FY28 and reviewed two scenarios for the department operating budget, one of which would cut staff hours if a town override fails. Additionally, the board approved a 6-foot foundation setback variance for a commercial septic pump chamber at 250 Turnpike Road in a 2-1 vote and previewed its October flu clinic schedule.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved the amended minutes of the August 11, 2026 meeting.
key_details: The chair corrected the August 11 minutes to reflect a vote against a Newton Street variance rather than in favor.

topics.title: Statewide kratom ban and local retail review
topics.summary: Substance use prevention coordinator Emily Tylyk presented an overview of kratom in light of recent Massachusetts Department of Public Health actions. Effective August 28, 2026, Massachusetts designated kratom as a Schedule I controlled substance under a one-year temporary order, granting municipalities authority to ensure its removal from retail shelves. Staff reported that only one retailer in Southborough was found carrying a small display of kratom products, and other retailers were unaware of the substance.
key_details: Kratom is classified as a Schedule I controlled substance in Massachusetts under a one-year order.
Retailers must secure and inventory remaining stock and either return it to distributors or arrange lawful disposal.
Only one retailer in Southborough was found selling kratom, and staff provided education to local businesses.
State guidance and addiction resources are available at mass.gov/kratom.
topics.outcome: Information presented with no board action needed.

topics.title: FY28 elected Board of Health budget
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved the FY28 budget line for elected board members.
key_details: The budget line covers stipends of $150 per board member for three members.
Total budget approved is $450, unchanged from previous years.

topics.title: FY28 Health Department operating budget scenarios
topics.summary: The department presented two FY28 budget options in accordance with Select Board guidance. Request A represents a level-service budget of $329,835 with 5 percent wage increases approved by the Personnel Board, while Request B models a zero-percent increase over FY27 in the event a town override is declined. To achieve a zero-percent increase under Request B, staff proposed reducing weekly hours for three staff members and eliminating in-state travel and training funds.
key_details: Request A totals $329,835, which includes 5 percent wage and COLA adjustments.
Request B achieves a 0 percent increase over FY27 by cutting weekly staff hours: 1 hour for the administrative assistant, 2 hours for the director, and 30 minutes for the sanitarian.
Northborough reimburses Southborough for 50 percent of the shared health agent salary, though that revenue goes into the general fund.
Staff noted that the department operating budget has decreased over the past five years through shared staffing arrangements.
topics.outcome: Vote deferred; the board will draft an explanatory memo to the Select Board and vote on the final request at its next meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: If the town does not pass an operating override, cuts to Health Department staff hours could lead to delays in municipal septic reviews and public health services.

topics.title: Septic pump chamber variance for 250 Turnpike Road
topics.summary: Engineer James Tetreault presented a plan for 250 Turnpike Road to replace a failing, deteriorated sewer pipe hung under a footbridge with a new pump chamber and force main. Because of site constraints and a required 25-foot wetland setback, the applicant requested a variance from the standard 10-foot building foundation setback to place the pump chamber 6 feet from the building wall. The board approved the 6-foot variance with a vapor barrier condition, while noting that the broader replacement plan and leaching area must still be reviewed with DEP and the Conservation Commission.
key_details: Property is located at 250 Turnpike Road, also known as the Beehive building.
Applicant requested a 6-foot setback from the building foundation instead of the standard 10 feet under Title 5.
A 40-mil impermeable vapor barrier will be installed along the building foundation to prevent any gas migration.
The project will require a temporary crossing and Notice of Intent approval from the Conservation Commission.
The board separately authorized department health agents and the sanitary inspector to sign the variance paperwork.
topics.outcome: Variance approved 2-1 (Liz Zadek voting against). Signing authorization passed 3-0.
topics.why_it_matters: The variance allows the commercial property to abandon a damaged sewer line over a wetland and construct an upgraded septic connection without encroaching closer to protected wetland boundaries.

topics.title: Fall flu clinic schedule
topics.summary: Department staff provided an overview of upcoming flu vaccination clinics scheduled for October.
key_details: Regional drive-through clinic with the Greater Boroughs will take place Saturday, October 3, from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM.
Senior clinic scheduled for October 7 at the Senior Center, with approximately 150 seniors anticipated.
Clinics for municipal staff, all public school staff, daycares, and the Fire Department will occur across the first two full weeks of October.
topics.outcome: Information shared with no vote required.

votes.motion: Approve the FY28 510 Elected Board of Health budget of $450.
Grant a 6-foot foundation setback variance for the pump chamber at 250 Turnpike Road.
Authorize the Health Department health agents and sanitary inspector to sign the variance for 250 Turnpike Road on behalf of the Board of Health.
